nodes.summary: For nonnegative weights and any `x` with `x s = 0` and `x t = 1`, `C_eff(s, t) ≤ xᵀ L x` (D. A. Spielman, *Spectral and Algebraic Graph Theory*, draft of 2 April 2025, Section 12.2).
nodes.title: Every admissible potential bounds the effective conductance

nodes.summary: If `0 ≤ w ≤ w'` edgewise, then the effective conductance between any two vertices for the weights `w` is at most that for `w'`: lowering conductances (raising resistances) cannot increase an effective conductance (D. A. Spielman, *Spectral and Algebraic Graph Theory*, draft of 2 April 2025, Theorem 12.3.1).
nodes.title: Rayleigh's monotonicity law

nodes.summary: Effective conductance is nonnegative for nonnegative weights.
nodes.title: Effective conductance is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For edge weights `w`, the infimum of the Laplacian energy `xᵀ L x` over all potentials `x` with `x s = 0` and `x t = 1`, i.e. twice the minimum spring energy when `s` and `t` are held at distance one (D. A. Spielman, *Spectral and Algebraic Graph Theory*, draft of 2 April 2025, Section 12.2, where it is written `C_eff(s, t)`). It is `0` when `s = t`, where no potential is admissible.
nodes.title: Effective conductance

nodes.summary: If `0 ≤ w ≤ w'` edgewise and the effective conductance between `s` and `t` is positive for `w`, then the effective resistance between them for `w'` is at most that for `w`: raising resistances cannot decrease an effective resistance (D. A. Spielman, *Spectral and Algebraic Graph Theory*, draft of 2 April 2025, the remark after Theorem 12.3.1).
nodes.title: Rayleigh's monotonicity law for effective resistance

nodes.summary: For nonnegative weights and distinct vertices `s` and `t`, if the potentials `v` satisfy `L v = δ_s - δ_t` (one unit of current injected at `s` and extracted at `t`), then the effective resistance between `s` and `t` is `v(s) - v(t)`, and this number is positive. nodes.title: Effective resistance is a potential difference

nodes.summary: The reciprocal of the effective conductance (D. A. Spielman, *Spectral and Algebraic Graph Theory*, draft of 2 April 2025, Section 12.2, `R_eff(s, t) = 1 / C_eff(s, t)`). With Lean's convention `0⁻¹ = 0` it is `0` when the effective conductance vanishes, for instance between different connected components.
nodes.title: Effective resistance

nodes.summary: In a connected loopless multigraph with positive weights on `n` vertices, `∑_e w_e R_eff(e) = n - 1`. can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
